dispatch.title: Before peace decides the race
dispatch.subtitle: 24 October 2026 · Immediate project counterplay
dispatch.summary: When a rival is one turn from victory, a binding peace can end the race. An available company should keep its chance to interrupt the project before that turn advances.
takeaways: Review a visible imminent enemy project against an immediately legal siege, or maintain an own siege already pausing it, before accepting or proposing binding peace.
Reject and interrupt in one planning round, then preserve the pause when fresh peace arrives; a strictly sooner own project remains a reason to take peace.
This is bounded AI choice over ordinary commands. Wider counterplay, campaign pacing and all fifteen release gates remain open.

sections.title: One chance before the treaty
paragraphs: In a retained authored regression, an enemy company stood beside a prosperity host with its project four of five turns complete. An ordinary siege could pause it immediately. Instead, the AI proposed or accepted ten turns of white peace because the war had lasted long enough, and the project won on the next turn.

The candidate protects that available response. It reviews imminent enemy projects with a currently observed host: a suitable uncommitted adjacent army can establish a legal siege, or an existing own siege can keep an already paused project from resuming under peace. A public project announcement alone is not an attack opportunity.

A separate authored control gives the defending realm an active project that finishes strictly sooner. Accepting peace can then win its own race. Equal remaining times and paused own projects do not establish that exception.

sections.title: The same round matters
paragraphs: The retained setup authors infrastructure, starting budgets and an adjacent guard, then uses ordinary commands for research, institutions, project purchase, war duration and four active project turns. It does not inject project progress or claim to explain the headline campaigns.

The real worker plans each realm once before advancing a turn. Rejecting peace and relying on a hypothetical second plan is too late with one turn remaining. The candidate instead returns the ordinary rejection and one prevalidated siege together. A retained command probe confirms that the rejection leaves the relevant siege facts unchanged; each submitted command still undergoes canonical validation.

Four built-production browser journeys pass through public controls with development hooks absent. Player End turn establishes the immediate interruption. Both Watch branches run five full rounds and reject a fresh turn-30 offer, retaining the siege and paused four-of-five project through turn 31. On the fifth round, one real battle ends in mutual withdrawal and Ashen wins on turn 32; the other captures the host and cancels its project. Every intermediate export replays, and final manual save/reload preserves the exact archive. Counterplay is an opportunity, not a guaranteed combat win.

sections.title: Legal orders, limited sight
paragraphs: The simulation owns a siege-establishment quote that shares the existing command legality checks and refusal order. A movement preview identifying a settlement does not establish siege legality. The quote uses permitted observations, makes no path search and does not clone hidden campaign state.

Modern observations expose the agreed capability and a neutral strategic-command blocker when a global battle, capture or victory prevents the order. They reveal no private combat participants or locations. Older observations retain their former policy decisions; rules/save and canonical treaty semantics remain unchanged in this candidate.

The AI preserves routes, postings, delegated actors, missions and protected diplomatic relationships, and excludes unsuitable or exhausted companies and a force plainly weaker than the observed host garrison. It reviews at most eight project candidates and makes four establishment queries in stable order. No-offer review also runs during offer cooldown, preventing a rejected treaty from leaving the available interruption unused.

sections.title: Keep the decision in the record
paragraphs: The reused chronicle illustration comes from the 21 September Short Watch regression. It shows the existing technical record and its saved continuation, not this project interruption or a new victory outcome. Its original native PNG, historical caption and provenance remain unchanged; this dispatch adds no image inventory.

The actual project desktop and 390px/130%-text screenshots are retained with the browser review and exact command archives. The desktop shows the initial pause; final Watch narrow views show completion after combat withdrawal and cancellation after occupation. The images are native scrolled Realm affairs viewports, not proof of the whole AI or save-integrity gate.

sections.title: Measure the correction
paragraphs: The final maintained-siege candidate passes the full local suite: 2,304 tests across 280 files, with typecheck and production build passing. Four final browser journeys pass; their 17.0-second duration is execution metadata because outcome-only pacing overlapped, not a performance claim. The first extended run retained a modal-blocked export failure; the test now closes the actual victory chronicles through its public control. Final benchmark measurements and the implementation source pin remain pending.

All nine final headline campaign hashes match the retirement baseline exactly: Standard 219/194/201, Long 329/309/287 and Epic 374/332/327. Two Epic seeds still finish early; this is unchanged measured behavior, not overall pacing acceptance. No prices or proxy bounds changed to make the result green. Final planner timings must keep their fixture scope and exclusions visible.

sections.title: The work still ahead
paragraphs: This advances existing AI competency and contestable-victory work without adding or removing gameplay scope. It establishes no new victory path, long-range operation planner or general treaty valuation. It maintains an own observed siege that is already pausing an imminent project; hidden hosts, distant armies, unavailable forces, and pauses without that own siege remain outside this response. Real battle losses can still allow a rival to complete.

R06, DH-021 and all fifteen release gates remain open. Final publication still needs exact implementation and deployment identities, independent source and factual review, integrated browser evidence and campaign measurement. Deployment is a development checkpoint, not 1.0 acceptance.
